name: Maharashtra Police Citizen Portal — Search & View Published FIR
publisher: Maharashtra Police / Home Dept, Govt of Maharashtra (CCTNS)
lag: days — FIRs appear within days of registration
caveats: Published FIRs EXCLUDE sensitive categories by policy — rape/POCSO/women-and-child cases are withheld, so the feed systematically undercounts exactly the crimes users most want mapped
Sections strings are Marathi Devanagari ('भारतीय न्याय संहिता (बी एन एस), 2023 - 303(2)'), needing transliteration + section->category mapping
IPC->BNS break at 2024-07-01: pre-July-2024 rows carry IPC sections, later rows BNS. Series is not continuous
Geo unit is the POLICE STATION, not the incident location. No incident lat/lon is published — mapping these as points implies a precision the data does not have
ASP.NET __VIEWSTATE/__EVENTVALIDATION must be replayed per request; wide date ranges time out, so harvest in narrow windows per station
'hasDownloadButton' was false for all 500 rows in the sample checked — FIR PDF availability is partial, not universal
No published ToU or robots exemption reviewed; legality of bulk re-publication is untested
evidence: Could not fetch the portal (egress 403). Verified indirectly and strongly: downloaded 500 real harvested rows from github.com/Atharvayadav11/mahagovscrapper (fir-data-2025-09-27...json) with fields srNo/state/district/policeStation/year/firNumber/registrationDate/firNoWithYear/sections/hasDownloadButton — e.g. NASHIK CITY / ADAGAON POLICE STATION / FIR 0258/2025 / 11-08-2025 17:52:50 / BNS 303(2). THREE independent codebases (Atharvayadav11/mahagovscrapper fir-scraper.js, RudraBhagat/FIR_Agent services/scraper.py, PALASH2201/web_scraping pdf_data.py) all post to this URL with NO captcha and NO login.
how_to_obtain: HTTP POST to PublishedFIRs.aspx replaying __VIEWSTATE/__EVENTVALIDATION/__PREVIOUSPAGE. Controls: ctl00$ContentPlaceHolder1$ddlDistrict (numeric code, e.g. 19408), $ddlPoliceStation, $txtDateOfRegistrationFrom, $txtDateOfRegistrationTo (dd/MM/yyyy), $txtFirno, $btnSearch, $ucRecordView$ddlPageSize (50). Page via __EVENTTARGET=ctl00$ContentPlaceHolder1$ucGridRecordView, __EVENTARGUMENT=Page$N. FIR PDF = input button in result cell index 9.
notes: THE single most valuable source in this scope. Station-level, second-resolution timestamps, statewide, daily, open. Registration timestamps enable time-of-day/day-of-week safety analysis no other western-state source supports.

name: Maharashtra Citizen Portal — Search Accused / Information of Arrested Accused
caveats: Names arrested individuals — presumption of innocence. Republishing identifiable arrestee data is a serious legal/ethical exposure and should NOT be mapped
Arrest != conviction != crime occurrence; cannot be summed with FIR counts
evidence: URL (note the official typo 'Searcg') appears as a live link in a real captured copy of mumbaipolice.gov.in I downloaded from github.com/VidhaanShahh/RoadSOS (data/raw/mumbai_police_stations.html), alongside the PublishedFIRs link. Mumbai Police menu labels it 'Information of Arrested Accused'.
how_to_obtain: Same ASP.NET POST pattern as PublishedFIRs.aspx.
notes: Use only as a denominator/outcome signal in aggregate. Do not publish person-level.

name: Crime in Maharashtra (annual) — CID Maharashtra
publisher: Criminal Investigation Department, Maharashtra State (Statistical Branch), Pune
time_latest: unknown — 2017 is the only edition positively identified
caveats: PDF tables; likely needs OCR/table extraction
District/commissionerate reorganisation breaks the series
NCRB principal-offence-rule style counting likely applies
Only the 2017 edition was positively identified; continuity to present unconfirmed
evidence: Search index returned the title 'CRIME IN MAHARASHTRA- 2017 Criminal Investigation Department Maharashtra State' for the 486.pdf URL, and a 'Crime in Maharashtra | MAHACID' publications landing page. Not fetched — egress 403 on both hosts.
notes: The benchmark series to validate scraped FIR counts against. Establishes whether the portal feed is complete.

name: Mumbai Police — Crime Review / Crime Statistics
publisher: Mumbai Police (Commissioner of Police, Greater Mumbai)
caveats: City-total tables, not station-level — do not assume the page name implies granularity
Mumbai city police jurisdiction != BMC municipal boundary; Thane/Navi Mumbai are separate commissionerates
evidence: Both paths confirmed present in the Mumbai Police site navigation in a real captured copy of the site (RoadSOS repo), and returned by search with titles 'Crime Statistics | Mumbai Police' and 'Crime Review | Mumbai Police'.
notes: Cross-check for the FIR scrape over the same months.

name: Mumbai Police — per-police-station pages with embedded map coordinates
caveats: Coordinates come from an embedded Google Maps iframe, so they are the station's pin, not a jurisdiction polygon
No station BOUNDARY polygons are published anywhere — this is the core cartographic gap for a police.uk-style map
evidence: Downloaded real captures of these pages (RoadSOS data/raw/mumbai_police_station_pages/policestation_ps_*.html, ps_2..ps_95 => ~95+ stations). policestation_ps_20.html contains a Google Maps embed encoding !2d72.81654191437444!3d18.911938662 — i.e. extractable lat 18.9119 / lng 72.8165 per station.
how_to_obtain: Iterate ps=1..~100, regex the maps embed for !2d<lng>!3d<lat>.
notes: Gives genuine per-station coordinates for Mumbai — far better than the crude geocoding in the scraper corpus.

name: Pune City Police — Crime Statistics / Crime Review
caveats: Granularity unconfirmed — assume city totals until a table is actually opened
punepolice.gov.in and admin.punepolice.gov.in both resolve; admin.* is the live CMS
evidence: Search returned titles 'Crime Statistics | Pune City Police' and 'Crime Review | Pune City Police' for these admin.punepolice.gov.in paths. Not fetched (egress 403).
notes: Pune is a strong pilot city: city stats + rural stats + a data.gov.in catalogue + ICCC all coexist.

name: Pune Rural Police — Crime Statistics / Crime Review
caveats: Rural district excludes Pune city commissionerate — the two must be unioned and never double-counted
evidence: Search returned 'Crime Statistics' and 'Crime Review' page titles on puneruralpolice.gov.in. Not fetched.
notes: Demonstrates the Maharashtra district-police CMS pattern: /crime-statistics and /crime-review paths recur across district sites.

name: Maharashtra district police websites (Palghar, Chandrapur, et al.) — per-district crime pages
caveats: Coverage and freshness vary wildly per district; many such sites are stale
Each district runs its own CMS instance — no uniform schema
evidence: palgharpolice.gov.in ('Home | Palghar Police') and chandrapurpolice.gov.in ('Chandrapur Police | Home') returned as live titles by search. The /crime-statistics + /crime-review path pattern is shared with puneruralpolice.gov.in.
notes: Worth a systematic sweep in Phase 2: enumerate all ~45 Maharashtra units and probe the two known paths.

name: Maharashtra CCTNS NCL Dashboard (CCTNS.STATE.CAS)
caveats: Credentialed police-internal dashboard; no public access route identified
Do not attempt to access without authorisation
evidence: Search returned the title 'CCTNS.STATE.CAS' for this Login.aspx URL on the same host as the public citizen portal.
how_to_obtain: Not obtainable openly. Route is an official MoU/data-sharing request to Maharashtra DGP office, or an RTI asking what aggregate reports the dashboard can export.
notes: Evidence that station-level aggregates already exist in exportable form internally — strengthens an RTI/partnership ask.

name: Crimes in Pune — OGD Platform India catalogue
caveats: data.gov.in city catalogues are frequently stale, sometimes a one-off upload years old
Granularity claim unverified — could be city totals rather than station-wise
evidence: Catalogue URL returned by search under 'Crime Statistics' dataset group; described as an indicator of prevalent crime rate in a city released under NDSAP. Host blocked by egress policy, not opened.
notes: If this is genuinely station-wise it is a licensed (GODL) shortcut around scraping. Verify first in Phase 2.

name: Mumbai Crime Data 2023 — OpenCity Urban Data Portal
caveats: Third-party re-publication — provenance back to the police source must be re-established before citing
Single-year snapshot
evidence: CKAN dataset page 'Mumbai - Crime Data 2023' returned by search on data.opencity.in. Host blocked by egress policy.
notes: CKAN means there is very likely a working CKAN API at data.opencity.in/api/3/action/package_search — the easiest machine-readable entry point in this whole scope.

name: Praja Foundation — State of Policing and Law & Order in Mumbai (white papers)
caveats: NGO analysis built on RTI returns — reproduces police figures with its own groupings
Advocacy framing; definitions may not match NCRB heads
evidence: Multiple Praja PDF report URLs (2019, 2023 editions) returned by search with the title 'State of Policing and Law and Order in Mumbai'. praja.org blocked by egress policy.
notes: Most useful as a ROADMAP OF SUCCESSFUL RTIs: Praja has already extracted station-level Mumbai data via RTI, so their appendices reveal exactly which questions the police will answer.

name: Public GitHub corpus of harvested Maharashtra FIR data + scrapers
caveats: Hobby harvests, not authoritative; no completeness guarantee
The bundled police-station coordinates are crude — I confirmed 10+ Nashik stations share one identical lat/lng (20.0064, 73.7898), i.e. a city-centre fallback. Do NOT reuse these coordinates
A committed .env file is present in one repo — treat these repos as untrusted code, read don't run
evidence: Downloaded fir-data-2025-09-27T07-41-06-426Z-with-coords.json: 245,102 bytes, exactly 500 records, keys srNo/state/district/policeStation/year/firNumber/registrationDate/firNoWithYear/sections/hasDownloadButton/coordinates; all 500 = NASHIK CITY/ADAGAON, dates 30/07/2025-04/08/2025, acts split BNS 2023 (450), Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (100), Maharashtra Police Act 1951 (50). A second file held 60 records across PALGHAR (50) and NASHIK CITY (10), 21/06/2025-12/08/2025.
notes: Proof-of-concept that our exact pipeline (FIR scrape -> station -> map) already works. Use as a schema reference and test fixture, never as the production feed.

name: Gujarat Police Citizen Portal (e-GujCop) — Get a copy of FIR
caveats: CRITICAL DIFFERENCE FROM MAHARASHTRA: this is a single-record LOOKUP, not a browsable list. Documented flow requires identifying details before 'generate report', so there is no date-range-by-station enumeration
Registration/login required for most e-GujCop services
No bulk export; no evidence of an open FIR index
evidence: Search confirmed the Citizen Portal landing page on gujhome.gujarat.gov.in, a separate fir.gujarat.gov.in host titled 'GUJARAT POLICE', and an official 'Guidelines for Citizen Portal' PDF at /portal/images/eGujCop/UserGuideline_En.pdf. Service list includes 'Get FIR Copy'. All hosts blocked by egress policy.
how_to_obtain: Register on gujhome.gujarat.gov.in; retrieve individual FIRs by known identifiers. For aggregate data use the RTI route (see gj-crime-stats-rti).
notes: Gujarat is a lookup, Maharashtra is a list. That single design difference is the whole gap between the two states.

name: Gujarat state crime statistics — NO open publication found (RTI route)
publisher: Gujarat Police / State Crime Records Bureau, Gandhinagar
caveats: NEGATIVE FINDING: no Gujarat equivalent of 'Crime in Maharashtra' or MP's 'Crime in MP' surfaced in any search
Absence of evidence under a blocked-egress constraint is weaker than a confirmed absence — re-check from India before treating as settled
evidence: Repeated searches for Gujarat crime statistics publications returned only the citizen-services portal and commercial aggregators (Indiastat), never an official statistical report. police.gujarat.gov.in blocked by egress policy so its Downloads/RTI section was never opened.
how_to_obtain: RTI to the Public Information Officer, Director General of Police, Gujarat, Police Bhavan, Sector 18, Gandhinagar. Ask for: district-wise and police-station-wise counts of FIRs registered by major head, monthly, last 5 years, in machine-readable (XLSX/CSV) form, and cite that CCTNS already holds it electronically so no disproportionate diversion of resources applies.
notes: Also check the Gujarat SCRB and the state Home Dept RTI proactive-disclosure (Sec 4(1)(b)) page before filing. Formats not recorded by the researching agent; confirm during the URL verification pass.

name: Crime in Madhya Pradesh — SCRB, MP Police
publisher: State Crime Records Bureau, Madhya Pradesh Police, Bhopal
caveats: Annual district aggregates only — no station-level, no monthly
PDF tables likely needing extraction
MP has repeatedly created new districts; district series break
evidence: Search returned this exact path with the title 'Madhya Pradesh Police - SCRB Bhopal ... Official SCRB MP Police Website'. The SCRB is described as annually releasing state crime statistics. Host blocked by egress policy.
notes: MP's best open source. Equivalent in kind to 'Crime in Maharashtra' — the benchmark layer, not the map layer.

name: MP Police Citizen Portal — View FIR (CitizenService 13)
caveats: Gated behind CitizenLogin.aspx — unlike Maharashtra there is no anonymous published-FIR list
Scraping behind a personal login would breach portal ToU and is not a viable production route
evidence: URL appears in a third-party state-FIR-portal index (github.com/Mehul-Rathva/osint-toolkit-central-main, src/pages/StateFirPortals.tsx) which I downloaded; the file notes 'Some portals may require registration or login'. The CitizenLogin.aspx path is itself the evidence of gating.
how_to_obtain: Citizen registration gives single-record access only. For bulk, RTI to SCRB MP (see mp-scrb-crime-in-mp) or a formal data-sharing request to MP DGP.
notes: Same ASP.NET CCTNS stack as Maharashtra — so the data model is identical; only the publication policy differs. That makes MP a strong RTI target: ask them to publish what Maharashtra already publishes.

name: Crime in Chhattisgarh — CG Police
caveats: Granularity unconfirmed and possibly narrative rather than tabular — treat as state-level until a table is opened
Cited conservatively as `state` per the spec rule that an unopened claim does not earn a fine granularity label
evidence: Search returned the dedicated path cgpolice.gov.in/crime-in-chhattisgarh and the official site title 'Official website of the Chhattisgarh Police, Government of Chhattisgarh, India'. Host blocked by egress policy.
notes: Lowest-effort first check for CG in Phase 2.

name: Chhattisgarh CCTNS Citizen Portal — View FIR
caveats: Java/JSP CCTNS build (differs from Maharashtra's ASP.NET), gated at Citizen_Login.jsp
Two hosts serve the same app (dashboard.cgpolice.gov.in and search.cgpolice.gov.in) — unclear which is canonical
evidence: Search returned 'View FIR | CG Police' for Citizen_Login.jsp on both dashboard.cgpolice.gov.in and search.cgpolice.gov.in, plus a Citizen_Portal.jsp landing page. Corroborated by the StateFirPortals.tsx index I downloaded. Hosts blocked by egress policy.
how_to_obtain: Citizen registration for single records; RTI to CG SCRB for aggregates.
notes: Worth probing whether any JSP endpoint is reachable pre-login — JSP CCTNS builds elsewhere sometimes expose an unauthenticated FIR list.

name: Chhattisgarh LWE / Naxal incident data — no open state feed (RTI / MHA route)
caveats: NEGATIVE FINDING: no public incident-level LWE dataset from CG Police surfaced
Security-sensitive category — expect RTI exemption under Sec 8(1)(a) RTI Act (sovereignty/security) for incident-level detail
LWE incidents are counted under a bespoke MHA taxonomy that does not map onto IPC/BNS heads, so they cannot be merged into a general crime map without a separate layer
Mapping LWE incidents carries real-world safety and political risk — recommend excluding from a consumer safety map
evidence: Searches on CG Police surfaced only general Naxalism context (Wikipedia/CG Police 'about' framing), never a dataset or incident register. No candidate URL found.
how_to_obtain: District-wise annual LWE violence tables appear in the MHA Annual Report (mha.gov.in) — that is the practical open source. For state detail, RTI to PIO, DGP Chhattisgarh, Police Headquarters, Naya Raipur, expecting partial Sec 8(1)(a) refusal.
notes: Recommend scoping OUT of v1. High risk, low product value for a 'is this neighbourhood safe to rent in' use case.

name: Goa Police Citizen Portal — View FIR / FIR document search
caveats: Registration required: the portal states the FIR-viewing facility needs sign-in, with a Create Account option
Liferay portal (/web/guest/...), so a different stack again — no reuse of the Maharashtra scraper
Goa is small (~2 districts, ~30 stations) so absolute volumes are low and small-number effects will dominate any rate map
evidence: Search returned 'View Fir - GOA POLICE' at /web/guest/view-fir and a 'SCRB - GOA POLICE' page at /web/guest/scrb; the description states the portal lets users view FIRs registered by different police stations in Goa but requires registration. A distinct /web/guest/firdocsearch path appears in the StateFirPortals.tsx index I downloaded. Host blocked by egress policy.
how_to_obtain: Create a citizen account on citizen.goapolice.gov.in, then evaluate whether view-fir or firdocsearch permits station+date enumeration once inside. That single check decides whether Goa is a viable pilot.
notes: Best PILOT candidate after Maharashtra: small enough to validate the whole pipeline end-to-end, and it does list FIRs by police station. The open question is only whether the login gate also caps enumeration.

name: Goa SCRB — State Crime Records Bureau page
publisher: State Crime Records Bureau, Goa Police
caveats: SCRB's described role is compiling returns FOR NCRB's 'Crime in India', so this may be a description page with no downloadable state tables
A 'Download Forms' page is service forms, not data — do not mistake it for a data download
evidence: Search returned 'SCRB - GOA POLICE' and 'Download Forms - GOA POLICE' pages; the SCRB text references compiling annual 'Crime in India' and Accidental Deaths & Suicides data. Not fetched.
notes: Check whether Goa SCRB publishes its own state volume or only feeds NCRB.

name: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu Police — website and citizen portal
publisher: Police Department, UT of DNH & DD
geo_coverage: UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
caveats: Described function is service requests and status tracking — NOT a published FIR list
Two legacy domains (dnhpolice.gov.in, and the merged ddd.gov.in) coexist post-UT-merger; the old DNH host is http-only
UT population ~600k across three non-contiguous enclaves — any map here is a handful of stations and statistically thin
evidence: Search returned 'Homepage | Police Department, Dadra Nagar Haveli & Daman Diu' at police.ddd.gov.in, a citizen-portal service page, and legacy hosts dnhpolice.gov.in / citizen.dnhpolice.gov.in. The portal is described as CCTNS service-request and status tracking. No crime statistics surfaced.
how_to_obtain: RTI to the PIO, Superintendent of Police, DNH at Silvassa and SP Daman — two separate PIOs despite the merged UT.
notes: Lowest priority in scope. Include for national completeness, not for product value.

name: DNH & DD crime statistics — NO published data found (RTI route)
publisher: UT Administration of DNH & DD, Home Department
caveats: NEGATIVE FINDING: no crime statistics publication of any kind surfaced for this UT
NCRB 'Crime in India' remains the only reliable series covering this UT
evidence: Searches across police.ddd.gov.in, ddd.gov.in/police, dnh.gov.in and dnhpolice.gov.in returned helpline and service pages only — no statistics, no annual report, no dashboard.
how_to_obtain: RTI to PIO, Home Department, UT Administration of DNH & DD, Secretariat, Silvassa 396230, requesting station-wise FIR counts by major head, monthly, last 5 years, in CSV/XLSX.
notes: For this UT, fall back to NCRB state/UT tables rather than chasing a local source. Formats not recorded by the researching agent; confirm during the URL verification pass.

name: Digital Police Portal — national index of State Police Citizen Portals
caveats: An index of links, not data
Link rot is common as states migrate CCTNS hosts
evidence: Search returned the page titled 'State Police Citizen Portals' at this path. Host blocked by egress policy (confirmed 403 CONNECT for digitalpolice.gov.in).
notes: The authoritative way to resolve every state's CURRENT citizen-portal domain in one fetch — highest-leverage single page to open first in Phase 2.

name: Police Stations roster with lat/lon (CityName, Station, Address, Longitude, Latitude)
publisher: Smart Cities / data.gov.in open data (exact publisher unresolved)
geo_coverage: Indian cities (schema is national; the copy I opened held only Amaravati rows)
caveats: The copy I opened is a 433-byte, 3-row stub — the full national file was NOT obtained
The '_0' filename suffix is the data.gov.in resource convention, so the real source is almost certainly an OGD/Smart Cities catalogue, but I could not confirm which
Semicolons are used as intra-field separators, which will break naive CSV parsing
evidence: Downloaded the file: 433 bytes, header exactly 'CityName,Name of Police Station,Address,Longitude,Latitude', 3 data rows all Amaravati/Andhra Pradesh, e.g. 'Police Station - Thullur, 16.51993327, 80.46642602'.
how_to_obtain: Search data.gov.in for the 'Police Stations' resource carrying this exact header to recover the full national file.
notes: Schema is exactly what we need to geolocate station-level FIR counts. Finding the complete version of this file is a high-value, low-cost Phase 2 task.
